jobs.title: Director, Assisted Channels Platform Strategy, Resiliency & Organizational Change Management
jobs.description:
About The Role

This is a unique opportunity to shape the strategy, resiliency and employee experience of the assisted-channel platforms that enable Personal & Business Banking (P&BB) employees to serve customers. Working across Business, Technology, Product, Operations and Risk teams, the Director will turn employee, customer and performance insights into clear priorities, roadmaps and sustained outcomes.

P&BB depends on assisted-channel platforms that are reliable, intuitive and able to evolve with employee and customer needs. This role will define how those platforms advance over time, how resiliency priorities are established and how change is introduced and sustained across the frontline.

This is a strategic and execution-focused mandate. The role connects near-term stability and employee-experience needs with longer-term platform modernization, ensuring that incidents, operational insights, adoption results and frontline feedback influence priorities and investment decisions.

The Director leads three integrated functions: Assisted Channels Platform Strategy and Resiliency, Organizational Change Management for Digital Employee Platforms, and BTE.
The role establishes the strategies, governance, measures and partnerships needed to improve technology performance, employee readiness and frontline outcomes. Acting as a trusted advisor and integrator, this individual works with senior leaders and delivery partners to establish shared accountability, resolve cross-functional barriers and provide clear recommendations on priorities, risks, sequencing and investment.

Key Responsibilities (not limited to):

Assisted Channels Platform Strategy & Resiliency

Own and continuously evolve the vision, target state, multi-year strategy and roadmap for P&BB assisted-channel platforms.
Translate business strategy, employee and customer needs, technology health and operational risk into sequenced priorities, investment recommendations and measurable outcomes.

Organizational Change Management

Own the integrated organizational change management strategy and roadmap for Digital Employee Platforms and technology change affecting P&BB and other lines of business.
Provide oversight of stakeholder engagement, impact assessment, communications, learning, readiness, adoption, sustainment and benefits realization.

Branch Technology Experience

Lead the business approach to improving the technology experience for P&BB frontline employees, with a focus on stability, usability, productivity and customer service.
Establish a consistent model for issue intake, triage, escalation, communication and follow-through in partnership with Enterprise Technology and Operations.

Cross-Functional & People Leadership

Act as the connective tissue across P&BB, Product, Technology, Operations and Risk, creating shared accountability for platform, change and employee-experience outcomes.
Represent the mandate in senior governance forums and provide concise recommendations, trade-offs and decisions required.

Additional Details:

Provides subject matter expertise in the design, development, management and implementation of assigned projects from business case development through execution. Works across BMO to deliver specific project/program business results in alignment with overall group goals.

Fosters a culture aligned to BMO purpose, values and strategy and role models BMO values and behaviours in all that they do.
Ensures alignment between values and behaviour that fosters diversity and inclusion.
Regularly connects work to BMO’s purpose, sets inspirational goals, defines clear expected outcomes, and ensures clear accountability for follow through.
Builds interdependent teams that collaborate across functional and operating groups to create the highest value for all stakeholders.
Attracts, retains, and enables the career development of top talent.
Improves team performance, recognizes and rewards performance, coaches employees, supports their development, and manages poor performance.
Acts as a trusted advisor to senior leaders for making business decisions and implementing strategic initiatives.
Develops an expert understanding of business/group challenges.
Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
Recommends measures to improve organizational effectiveness.
May consult to or serve on various committees and task forces.
Manages resources and leads the execution of strategic initiatives to deliver on business and financial goals.
Interacts with various BMO groups to ensure strategy and initiatives meet enterprise governance requirements.
Leads implementation of strategic initiatives within group and across BMO by partnering with various internal & external stakeholders as required; complexity of initiatives may vary and usually involve multiple stakeholders across the enterprise.
Defines business requirements for analytics & reporting to ensure data insights inform business decision making.
Provides coaching on complex strategic & business issues and facilitates processes to reach effective resolution.
Assesses and adapts existing operational programs; develops new capabilities to ensure ongoing success.
Leads the execution of operational programs; assesses and adapts as needed to ensure quality of execution.
Leads change management activities, ensuring cross business/group coordination and logistical support for the implementation of change.
Acts as a relationship manager on assigned projects/programs and ensures alignment to overall enterprise and group goals.
Develops solutions and makes recommendations based on an understanding of the business strategy and stakeholder needs.
Participates in project/program design and provides advice & subject matter expertise to achieve required business results.
Conducts analysis required to inform strategic recommendations and considers the “big picture” when assessing whether or not a course of action is advisable in terms of the group and enterprise goals.
Collaborates with internal & external stakeholders to provide business context in the design, develop and implementation of programs & solutions.
May network with industry contacts to gather and identify competitive insights and best practices.
Breaks down strategic problems, and analyses data and information to provide insights and recommendations.
Monitors and tracks performance, and addresses any issues.
Builds change management plans of varying scope and type; leads or participates in a variety of change management activities including readiness assessments, planning, stakeholder management, execution, evaluation and sustainment of initiatives.
Identifies enablers and key issues prior to and during implementation, raises issues with stakeholders and offers solutions to resolve issues or risks that jeopardize delivery.
Operates at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a senior specialist resource across BMO.
Influences how teams/groups work together.
Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to multiple, interdependent, complex problems.
Communicates abstract concepts in simple terms.
Fosters strong internal and external networks and works with and across multiple teams to achieve business objectives.
Anticipates trends and responds by implementing appropriate changes.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

Typically 10+ years of relevant experience and post-secondary degree in related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Demonstrated leadership experience in platform strategy, technology resiliency, organizational change, frontline operations, transformation, product delivery or a related discipline.
Proven experience defining multi-year strategies and roadmaps and influencing prioritization, investment and delivery decisions in a complex organization.
Experience in financial services, frontline banking or contact centres is an asset. Prosci, ADKAR or comparable organizational change management experience is also an asset.
Seasoned expert with extensive industry knowledge.
Technical leader viewed as a thought leader for innovation.
Verbal & written communication skills - Expert.
Analytical and problem solving skills - Expert.
Influence skills - Expert.
Collaboration & team skills; with a focus on cross-group collaboration - Expert.
Able to manage ambiguity.
Data driven decision making - Expert.

jobs.title: Director, Data Centre Strategy & Market Development*** Directeur(trice), stratégie des centres de données et développement des marches
jobs.description:
IPEX is one of North America’s leading providers of advanced plastic piping systems. Our mission is to shape a better tomorrow by connecting people with water and energy.

We currently have an exciting opportunity as a Director, Data Center Strategy & Market Development
This role is based is a hybrid in office Oakville, Ontario and reports to the Vice President, Transformation Office.

Do not miss the opportunity to join a diverse group of people-centric professionals, thought leaders, and rapid thinkers—entrepreneurs in spirit and status quo‑fighters.

Job Summary

The Director, Data Center Strategy & Market Development – North America will lead the development and execution of IPEX’s strategy to capture the rapidly growing data center opportunity across Canada and the United States.

Operating across IPEX’s traditional market segments, the Director will take an end-to-end view of the data center ecosystem, identifying where IPEX can create value across site infrastructure, building systems, cooling, water treatment and other emerging applications. The Director will define where IPEX should compete, develop the value proposition and portfolio roadmap required to win, and mobilize the organization behind a clear multi-year growth plan.

A critical component of the role will be developing relationships and influence with hyperscalers, colocation providers, engineering and design firms, developers, contractors, technology partners and other key decision-makers. The Director will work to position IPEX earlier in the design and specification process and increase the adoption of IPEX solutions within data center projects.

The role will be supported by a cross-functional team spanning Sales, Product Management, Innovation, Technical,Codes & Standards, Marketing and Operations .

Principal Responsibilities

Develop and own IPEX's North American data center strategy, defining priority applications, customers, geographies, technologies and routes to market and translating these into a multi-year growth roadmap.
Build an end-to-end view of the opportunity across site infrastructure, building systems, cooling systems, water treatment and other relevant applications, connecting opportunities across IPEX's existing segments and portfolios.
Develop deep understanding of the data center ecosystem and build senior relationships with hyperscale’s, colocation providers, engineers, developers, contractors and technology partners to understand requirements and influence material and system decisions.
Position IPEX upstream in the specification and design process, partnering with Technical and Codes & Standards to influence specifications, standards and acceptance of IPEX solutions.
Assess IPEX's current portfolio against evolving data center requirements and identify product, technology and capability gaps, recommending new product development, partnerships or other solutions required to compete.
Develop differentiated value propositions and solution positioning for priority applications, including mission-critical cooling and water-management systems.
Maintain strong awareness of emerging data center technologies and design trends, including direct liquid cooling, facility and technology cooling systems, water efficiency and evolving infrastructure requirements, and translate these into implications for IPEX.
Lead the cross-functional data center team, aligning Sales, Product Management, Innovation, Technical, Codes & Standards, Marketing and Operations around common priorities and execution plans.
Build market intelligence on project pipelines, competitors, technologies and customer requirements and translate insights into commercial priorities and investment recommendations.
Establish KPIs and regularly communicate progress, pipeline, strategic opportunities, risks and investment requirements to senior leadership.

Measures of Success

Clear North American data center strategy and multi-year growth roadmap established and executed.
Strong relationships developed with priority hyperscalers, colocation providers, engineering firms and other specification influencers.
Increased IPEX inclusion in data center designs and specifications.
Measurable pipeline and profitable incremental revenue generated across multiple IPEX segments.
Priority product and capability gaps identified and addressed through innovation, partnerships or portfolio development.
Differentiated IPEX value propositions established for priority applications, including cooling and water-management solutions.
Cross-functional resources aligned around a common set of data center priorities.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Marketing or a related discipline; advanced degree considered an asset.
10+ years of progressive experience in data centers, mission-critical infrastructure, building systems, cooling/HVAC, industrial systems, market development, product management or related fields.
Prior experience within the data center ecosystem strongly preferred, with demonstrated understanding of how hyperscalers, colocation providers, engineers and other stakeholders influence design, specification and purchasing decisions.
Existing relationships within the data center owner/operator, engineering, design or technology ecosystem would be a significant asset.
Ability to travel regularly throughout Canada and the United States.

IPEX is committed to providing accommodations for people with disabilities throughout the recruitment process and, upon request, will work with qualified job applicants to provide suitable accommodation in a manner that takes into account the applicant’s accessibility needs due to disability. Accommodation requests are available to candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process for IPEX jobs. To request an accommodation, please contact HR at HR@ipexna.com.

Ubisoft is a global leader in gaming with teams across the world creating original and memorable gaming experiences, from Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six to Just Dance and more. jobs.title: Director, Software Engineering (AI Workflows & Ecosystem)
jobs.description:
Are you driven to bring people, technology, and strategy together to build impactful software?

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber, they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

THE PROBLEM YOU’D OWN

Jobber has AI in production, but not yet at its full potential.

We already have AI answering calls, drafting responses, and powering parts of our product. But today, those systems are still fragmented. Some teams are ahead. Others aren’t. Some workflows are intelligent. Others are still manual. And most importantly, the system doesn’t yet think across the product.

A service pro still has to:

Manually follow up on jobs
Piece together context across workflows
Decide what to do next

The platform doesn’t proactively help them run their business. That’s the gap.

The opportunity is to evolve Jobber from: AI-powered features → AI-powered workflows → AI-powered business operations

This role owns that shift. Not a team. Not a feature. The system.

THE CUSTOMER

You’re building for people who don’t have time to think about software.

A plumber finishing their last job at 6 pm
A cleaner managing 30 clients and 5 employees
A landscaper juggling scheduling, payments, and follow-ups

They’re not asking for “AI.” They’re asking:

“What should I do next?”
“Why didn’t this job convert?”
“Who should I follow up with today?”

And eventually:

They shouldn’t have to ask at all.

The Director who succeeds here will understand:

This isn’t about building clever systems; it’s about building systems that remove thinking from already overwhelmed people.

What You’d Own

End-to-end ownership of Jobber’s AI system layer. You’re not owning a single team. You’re owning how intelligence flows across the entire product.

Product + Platform Scope

AI Foundations (models, orchestration, evals, guardrails)
Copilot (user-facing intelligence layer)
Automations (workflow execution layer)
Platform Experience / Marketplace (integration + ecosystem surface)
Emerging surfaces (voice, messaging, cross-product intelligence)

What This Actually Means

You are responsible for:

How decisions get made inside the system
How context moves across workflows
How actions get triggered (and when they shouldn’t)
How we evaluate whether AI is actually working

This includes:

Agentic workflows (reason → decide → act → evaluate)
Cross-product context (jobs, customers, payments, communication)
Reliability, safety, and failure modes
Developer experience for building on top of AI systems

Team Structure

~30 engineers across 4–6 teams
4–6 EMs / Sr EMs reporting into you
Close partnership with Product, Design, Data

What “good” Looks Like

Not “we shipped AI features.”

Instead:

The system proactively recommends and takes actions
Teams build on shared AI primitives, not reinventing them
AI output is reliable, measurable, and improving over time
Engineers trust the system, and move faster because of it
Customers feel like the product is working for them, not just responding

THE AI BAR (THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT)

We are not looking for:

Someone who rolled out Copilot internally
Someone who used LLM APIs for features
Someone adjacent to AI

We are looking for someone who has:

Built real systems where AI makes decisions and takes actions in production.

That means experience with:

Agent orchestration (not just prompts)
Tool use and workflow execution
Evaluation (offline + online)
Observability and failure handling
Guardrails and safety in real systems
Tradeoffs between autonomy vs. control

You don’t need to code daily, but you must be able to reason at the system level.

What You’ll Actually Do

Define how AI should work across Jobber, not just within a team
Build and evolve a multi-team org to execute on that vision
Make tradeoffs between speed, quality, and safety
Push teams beyond feature thinking into system thinking
Challenge assumptions, including leadership’s
Drive adoption across engineering, product, and the company

What We’re Looking For

Leadership

You’ve led orgs through complexity, not just growth.

Managed managers across multiple teams
Built organizations that scale (not just teams that ship)
Driven cross-org alignment in ambiguous spaces

Product + Systems Thinking

You think in systems, not features.

You understand how user workflows connect end-to-end
You’ve partnered deeply with Product and Design
You care about customer outcomes, not just technical output

AI Depth (non-negotiable)

You’ve built or led production LLM/agentic systems
.

You understand what actually works (and what doesn’t)
You’ve seen systems fail and improved them
You have opinions about evaluation, reliability, and safety

Execution

You can move fast without breaking everything.

You’ve balanced shipping vs infrastructure vs tech debt
You know when to iterate and when to redesign

WHY JOBBER

WHY NOW?

This is not “AI theatre.”

We already have:

AI Receptionist (live, handling real customer calls)
AI features embedded across the product
250,000+ businesses using the platform

What we don’t have yet is: A unified, intelligent system across the product.

That’s what this role builds.

TLDR:

Most Director roles optimize delivery. This one defines: How an entire product becomes intelligent.

What you can expect from Jobber:

A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.
A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.
A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.
To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.

A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

jobs.title: Director, Engineering and Procurement, AI Fabric
jobs.description:
Req Id:
432862

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell's AI Fabric initiative is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform, comprising seven large-scale, high-density data centres across the country, including a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2 GW flagship campus in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Reporting to the VP, Capital Programs, the Director, Engineering & Procurement is responsible for providing leadership across engineering governance, technical strategy, strategic sourcing, procurement, and supplier management for Bell's national AI Fabric portfolio. This role will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams while overseeing the procurement of mission-critical infrastructure, ensuring Bell secures and delivers the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, network, and modular systems required to support hyperscale AI operations. Working closely with Construction, Program Controls, Commissioning, Operations, Finance, Legal, and external partners, the Director will drive engineering excellence, commercial value, supply chain resilience, and successful project execution across a multi-billion-dollar capital program.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the engineering and procurement functions supporting Bell AI Fabric developments across multiple Canadian sites.
Establish engineering standards, technical specifications, design governance processes, and quality assurance frameworks for mission-critical infrastructure.
Oversee engineering reviews and approvals for power distribution, utility interconnections, backup generation, UPS systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, controls, and related systems.
Develop and execute procurement strategies for major capital equipment, engineering services, and long-lead infrastructure components required for AI data centre development.
Lead supplier selection, commercial negotiations, contract management, and strategic partnerships with OEMs, engineering firms, utilities, EPC contractors, and technology vendors.
Drive capacity planning, infrastructure resiliency, technology roadmaps, and technical risk mitigation strategies supporting high-density AI and GPU workloads.
Partner with Construction, Commissioning, Operations, and Program Controls teams to ensure engineering and procurement activities align with project schedules, budgets, and operational requirements.
Manage supply chain risks, supplier performance, cost optimization initiatives, and procurement governance across the portfolio.
Provide executive-level recommendations regarding infrastructure investments, commercial strategies, engineering risks, and project delivery performance.
Develop and lead a high-performing team while fostering a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Critical Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in engineering, procurement, construction, mission-critical facilities, data centres, energy infrastructure, or large-scale capital programs.
5+ years of people leadership experience managing engineering, procurement, project delivery, or integrated infrastructure teams.
Demonstrated experience delivering hyperscale data centres, mission-critical facilities, utility infrastructure, or large-scale industrial construction projects.
Strong technical expertise in electrical distribution systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, resiliency design, and mission-critical operations.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Strategic Business Executive
jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

________________________________________

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

________________________________________

Procurement Governance

Establish financial oversight and governance for procurement activities.
Ensure transparency, accountability, and value-for-money principles.
Develop policies and controls supporting major purchasing initiatives.
Participate in evaluation and approval processes for significant contracts and vendor relationships.
Ensure procurement activities align with Board-approved financial policies.

________________________________________

Indigenous Relations & Partnership Development

Build and maintain respectful relationships with Tsuut'ina Nation leadership and stakeholders.
Support initiatives that align with the Nation's economic development goals.
Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.
Ensure financial strategies reflect the values and long-term interests of ownership.

________________________________________

Stakeholder Management

The CFO Will Maintain Productive Relationships With

Internal Stakeholders

Board of Directors
Executive Leadership Team
Department Leaders
Team Members

External Stakeholders

Tsuut'ina Nation Leadership
Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC)
Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC)
Auditors
Financial Institutions
Legal Counsel
Development Partners
Government Agencies
Industry Associations
Consultants and Contractors

________________________________________

Risk Management & Governance

Lead enterprise risk management activities.
Ensure effective internal controls and compliance programs.
Support Board governance and Finance & Audit Committee activities.
Oversee annual external audits.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and accounting standards.
Develop financial risk mitigation strategies.

________________________________________

BOARD FINANCE & AUDIT COMMITTEE SUPPORT

The CFO serves as management's primary liaison to the Finance and Audit Committee and is responsible for:

Preparing committee materials and recommendations.
Presenting financial results and forecasts.
Supporting audit processes.
Monitoring risk management activities.
Reporting on compliance and internal controls.
Supporting governance best practices.

________________________________________

We thank all applicants, however, only those considered for an interview will be contacted.No phone calls please.

Priority will be given to Tsuut'ina Nation members.

new_jobs.description:
Req Id:
432862

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell's AI Fabric initiative is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform, comprising seven large-scale, high-density data centres across the country, including a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2 GW flagship campus in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Reporting to the VP, Capital Programs, the Director, Engineering & Procurement is responsible for providing leadership across engineering governance, technical strategy, strategic sourcing, procurement, and supplier management for Bell's national AI Fabric portfolio. This role will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams while overseeing the procurement of mission-critical infrastructure, ensuring Bell secures and delivers the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, network, and modular systems required to support hyperscale AI operations. Working closely with Construction, Program Controls, Commissioning, Operations, Finance, Legal, and external partners, the Director will drive engineering excellence, commercial value, supply chain resilience, and successful project execution across a multi-billion-dollar capital program.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the engineering and procurement functions supporting Bell AI Fabric developments across multiple Canadian sites.
Establish engineering standards, technical specifications, design governance processes, and quality assurance frameworks for mission-critical infrastructure.
Oversee engineering reviews and approvals for power distribution, utility interconnections, backup generation, UPS systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, controls, and related systems.
Develop and execute procurement strategies for major capital equipment, engineering services, and long-lead infrastructure components required for AI data centre development.
Lead supplier selection, commercial negotiations, contract management, and strategic partnerships with OEMs, engineering firms, utilities, EPC contractors, and technology vendors.
Drive capacity planning, infrastructure resiliency, technology roadmaps, and technical risk mitigation strategies supporting high-density AI and GPU workloads.
Partner with Construction, Commissioning, Operations, and Program Controls teams to ensure engineering and procurement activities align with project schedules, budgets, and operational requirements.
Manage supply chain risks, supplier performance, cost optimization initiatives, and procurement governance across the portfolio.
Provide executive-level recommendations regarding infrastructure investments, commercial strategies, engineering risks, and project delivery performance.
Develop and lead a high-performing team while fostering a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Critical Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in engineering, procurement, construction, mission-critical facilities, data centres, energy infrastructure, or large-scale capital programs.
5+ years of people leadership experience managing engineering, procurement, project delivery, or integrated infrastructure teams.
Demonstrated experience delivering hyperscale data centres, mission-critical facilities, utility infrastructure, or large-scale industrial construction projects.
Strong technical expertise in electrical distribution systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, resiliency design, and mission-critical operations.
Proven success leading strategic sourcing initiatives, complex commercial negotiations, and major procurement programs.
Deep understanding of engineering governance, capital project delivery, EPC contracting models, procurement practices, and commissioning processes.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, business case development, and contract administration.
Exceptional stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Construction Engineering, or a related technical discipline; P.Eng. designation strongly preferred.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and travel as required to support projects across Canada.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.
